title: Web Development Essentials
description: Test your knowledge of HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript, and web fundamentals.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element is semantically used to define the primary navigation links of a webpage?
questions.explanation: The <nav> tag is the HTML5 semantic standard specifically designed to hold primary navigation menus and link lists.

questions.question: In CSS Flexbox, which property is used to align items along the cross-axis?
questions.explanation: 'align-items' controls alignment along the cross-axis, whereas 'justify-content' aligns along the main-axis.

questions.question: What will be the output of `typeof null` in standard JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, `typeof null` returns 'object'. This is a historical quirk stemming from the first JS implementation where objects had a type tag of 0.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code signifies that a resource was successfully created on the server?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 201 indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between `let` and `var` in modern JavaScript (ES6+)?

options.text: Variables declared with `var` are block-scoped, while `let` is function-scoped.
Variables declared with `let` are block-scoped, while `var` is function-scoped.
`let` variables cannot be reassigned once declared.
`var` is hoisted without initialization, but `let` is never hoisted at all.

questions.explanation: `let` provides block scoping (confined within { ... }), whereas `var` is hoisted and function-scoped.

questions.question: Which Web API is commonly used in modern browsers to asynchronously send HTTP requests without page reloads?
questions.explanation: The Fetch API provides a modern, Promise-based interface for fetching resources asynchronously across the network.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the font-size of the root element (<html>)?
questions.explanation: 'rem' stands for Root EM and is relative to the root element's font size, whereas 'em' is relative to its immediate parent font-size.

questions.question: What will `[1, 2, 3] + [4, 5, 6]` evaluate to in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: The binary '+' operator converts both arrays to strings ('1,2,3' and '4,5,6') and concatenates them, producing '1,2,34,5,6'.

title: Python Programming Essentials
description: Assess your understanding of Python syntax, data types, functions, and standard libraries.

questions.question: Which of the following data structures in Python is immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples in Python are immutable; once instantiated, their elements cannot be altered, added, or removed.

questions.question: What is the output of the expression `bool([])` in Python?
questions.explanation: Empty collections in Python (like [], {}, set(), '') evaluate to False in boolean contexts.

questions.question: How do you correctly open a file in Python such that it automatically closes even if an error occurs?
questions.explanation: The 'with' statement creates a context manager that guarantees the file descriptor is closed when the block exits.

questions.question: What is the result of `2 ** 3 ** 2` in Python?
questions.explanation: The exponentiation operator `**` has right-to-left associativity: `3 ** 2 = 9`, then `2 ** 9 = 512`.

questions.question: Which built-in function returns both the index and value when iterating through a sequence?
questions.explanation: `enumerate(iterable)` yields tuples containing `(index, item)` for each element.

questions.question: What is a lambda function in Python?

options.text: A function that runs asynchronously in a background thread
A small anonymous function defined with the `lambda` keyword
A generator function that produces infinite streams
A built-in decorator for class methods

questions.explanation: Python's `lambda` keyword defines small, single-expression anonymous functions inline.

questions.question: What will `list(set([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]))` produce?
questions.explanation: Converting a list to a `set` eliminates all duplicate elements, and `list()` converts it back into a list with distinct values.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `__init__` in a Python class definition?

options.text: To destroy and garbage collect an object
To initialize the attributes of a newly created instance
To make the class private to the current module

questions.explanation: `__init__` is the constructor method in Python, automatically executed to initialize state when a class is instantiated.

title: Computer Science & Data Structures
description: Core concepts in algorithms, data structures, computational complexity, and logic.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST, each comparison halves the search space, giving an average search complexity of O(log n).

questions.question: Which data structure follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) operational principle?
questions.explanation: A Stack operates on the LIFO principle (the last element pushed is the first one popped).

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm achieves an optimal O(n log n) worst-case time complexity while also being stable?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort guarantees O(n log n) time in all cases (worst, average, best) and preserves the relative order of equal items (stability).

questions.question: In networking, which protocol provides reliable, connection-oriented, ordered byte-stream transmission?
questions.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) establishes a connection (3-way handshake) and provides error checking, sequence ordering, and acknowledgments.

questions.question: What occurs when two different keys hash to the exact same bucket index in a hash table?
questions.explanation: A hash collision happens when the hash function computes the same slot index for distinct inputs; resolved via chaining or open addressing.

questions.question: Which algorithmic design paradigm solves a problem by breaking it into overlapping subproblems and storing their solutions?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Programming optimizes recursive algorithms with overlapping subproblems by memoizing or tabulating intermediate subproblem results.

title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
description: Core principles of deep learning, supervised learning, neural networks, and model evaluation.

questions.question: Which machine learning paradigm uses labeled training datasets to learn a mapping function from input to output?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains predictive models using input-output pairs labeled with known correct answers.

questions.question: What is overfitting in machine learning models?

options.text: The model performs poorly on training data and well on test data
The model learns noise in training data and fails to generalize to unseen test data
The model trains too quickly due to high learning rate
The loss function reaches a global minimum too early

questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes random fluctuations in training data, resulting in high accuracy on training but poor generalization to unseen data.

questions.question: Which activation function is most widely used in hidden layers of deep neural networks to prevent vanishing gradients?
questions.explanation: ReLU, defined as f(x) = max(0, x), does not saturate in the positive region, allowing gradients to propagate efficiently through deep layers.

questions.question: In classification metrics, which formula evaluates Recall (Sensitivity)?
questions.explanation: Recall measures the proportion of actual positive samples that were correctly identified: TP / (TP + FN).

questions.question: What is the primary strength of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in image processing?

options.text: Exploiting spatial locality and translational invariance with parameter sharing
Generating discrete text embeddings without convolutions

questions.explanation: CNNs apply convolution kernels to capture local spatial relationships like edges and patterns, sharing weights across the input image.

questions.question: Which optimization technique updates neural network weights layer-by-layer backwards using the chain rule?
questions.explanation: Backpropagation calculates the gradient of the loss function with respect to each weight via calculus chain rule, propagating errors backwards.

title: Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking
description: Defensive security, encryption, common web vulnerabilities, authentication, and network defense.

questions.question: Which vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate backend database queries through unsanitized user input?
questions.explanation: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated directly into SQL command strings instead of using parameterized queries.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of asymmetric (public-key) cryptography?

options.text: It uses the same identical secret key for both encryption and decryption
It uses a mathematically linked pair: a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt
It can only encrypt files smaller than 128 bytes
It operates solely over wired physical connections

questions.explanation: Asymmetric encryption (e.g. RSA, ECC) employs a public key that anyone can use to encrypt data, and a private key held only by the receiver to decrypt.

questions.question: What is the security Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?

options.text: Systems must never use password credentials
Every user, program, or system should be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform its job
Firewalls must block all incoming and outgoing packets
Only senior managers can access computers

questions.explanation: Least Privilege limits blast radius: if an account or service is compromised, the attacker only inherits minimum necessary permissions.

questions.question: Which protocol provides cryptographic confidentiality, server authentication, and integrity for HTTP web traffic?
questions.explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS), powering HTTPS over TCP port 443, encrypts web exchanges and verifies server identity via digital certificates.

questions.question: Which social engineering attack lures victims into disclosing sensitive credentials by impersonating legitimate institutions?
questions.explanation: Phishing exploits human deception using spoofed emails, domain typosquatting, or fraudulent pages to harvest credentials.

questions.question: What are the three canonical authentication factors recognized in Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)?

options.text: Something you Know, Something you Have, and Something you Are
Something you See, Something you Say, and Something you Type
Email address, Phone number, and Home address

questions.explanation: MFA factors require: Knowledge (password/PIN), Possession (phone/security token), and Inherence (fingerprint/biometrics).

title: Database Systems & SQL
description: Relational databases, SQL queries, transaction ACID properties, indexing, and data normalization.

questions.question: What does the 'A' represent in the relational database ACID transaction guarantee?
questions.explanation: Atomicity ensures that all operations in a database transaction succeed together or the entire transaction rolls back ('all-or-nothing').

questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter aggregated data generated by a GROUP BY clause?
questions.explanation: 'WHERE' filters individual rows before aggregation; 'HAVING' filters group aggregates (e.g. HAVING COUNT(*) > 5) after grouping.

questions.question: Which SQL JOIN returns all rows from the left table, along with matching rows from the right table (filling NULL for missing matches)?
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table, pairing it with right-table columns when keys match or NULLs when they do not.

questions.question: Which indexing data structure is most widely adopted by SQL engines for disk-based table indexing?
questions.explanation: B+ Trees provide shallow balanced trees with high branching factor, minimizing disk I/O and enabling fast equality and range queries.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Database Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)?

options.text: Eliminating data redundancy and preventing insertion, update, and deletion anomalies

questions.explanation: Normalization breaks down large repetitive tables into smaller, well-structured relations linked by foreign keys to prevent data inconsistency.

questions.question: What is a key difference between a PRIMARY KEY and a UNIQUE constraint in SQL?

options.text: A table can have multiple PRIMARY KEYs, but only one UNIQUE constraint
A PRIMARY KEY strictly disallows NULL values, while UNIQUE constraints can accept NULLs
UNIQUE constraints can only apply to integer columns

questions.explanation: A table has at most one PRIMARY KEY which must be NOT NULL; tables can have multiple UNIQUE constraints which may allow NULL values.

title: Cloud Computing & DevOps
description: Containerization with Docker, Kubernetes orchestration, CI/CD pipelines, cloud architectures, and IaC.

questions.question: How do Docker containers fundamentally differ from traditional virtual machines (VMs)?

options.text: Containers require a complete guest operating system for each instance
Containers share the host OS kernel and run as lightweight isolated user processes
Containers can only run Python programs

questions.explanation: Containers virtualize at the operating system level, sharing the host kernel via cgroups and namespaces, while VMs virtualize hardware via a hypervisor.

questions.question: What is the primary function of Kubernetes in cloud environments?

options.text: Compiling source code into machine code
Automating containerized application deployment, autoscaling, load-balancing, and orchestration

questions.explanation: Kubernetes (K8s) provides declarative container orchestration across a cluster of nodes, handling self-healing, scaling, and rolling releases.

questions.question: What does the 'CI' acronym stand for in DevOps engineering?
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration (CI) is the practice of automatically integrating code into a shared repository and running builds/tests on every commit.

questions.question: Which zero-downtime deployment strategy maintains two identical environments (active production and staging) to switch traffic instantaneously?
questions.explanation: Blue-Green deployment runs the new version (Green) alongside the current version (Blue); once validated, router traffic redirects instantly with zero downtime.

questions.question: Which Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool uses declarative HCL configuration to provision resources across multi-cloud providers?
questions.explanation: HashiCorp Terraform enables developers to define and provision cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) declaratively with state tracking.

questions.question: What is the key distinction between Horizontal Scaling (Scale Out) and Vertical Scaling (Scale Up)?

options.text: Horizontal adds more servers/nodes to a pool; Vertical upgrades CPU/RAM on an existing server
Vertical adds more servers; Horizontal upgrades memory
Horizontal scaling requires shutting down servers permanently
Vertical scaling is only applicable to serverless functions

questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (Scale Out) distributes load across multiple machine instances, while Vertical scaling (Scale Up) increases the hardware capacity of one node.

title: Data Aptitude & Discrete Mathematics
description: Binary logic, discrete math, probability, combinatorics, modular arithmetic, and analytical problem-solving.

questions.question: What is the binary (Base-2) equivalent of the decimal integer 42?
What is the output of a standard 2-input XOR (Exclusive OR) logic gate when both inputs are 1 (True)?
questions.explanation: XOR outputs True (1) if and only if exactly one input is True. When both inputs are 1, the XOR output is 0 (False).

questions.question: What is the probability of drawing an Ace from a standard well-shuffled 52-card deck?
questions.explanation: There are 4 Aces in a 52-card deck: 4 / 52 simplifies to 1 / 13 (~7.69%).

questions.question: How many distinct 4-letter arrangements (permutations) can be formed using the letters in 'CODE' without repetition?
questions.explanation: Number of permutations for 4 distinct letters = 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

questions.question: What is the result of the modular arithmetic expression `29 mod 7`?
questions.explanation: 29 divided by 7 equals 4 with a remainder of 1 (7 × 4 + 1 = 29), so 29 mod 7 = 1.

questions.question: In an arithmetic progression defined by the formula a_n = 3n + 2, what is the value of the 10th term (a_10)?
